sections.kicker: Prepared for Latteria by Atla · November 2026
sections.lead: We looked at your Instagram the way a new customer would. Here is what stood out, in order of weight.
sections.thesis: Latteria won Asia's gelato title. Its front door still talks like the hype it says it ignores.
sections.keep: Your bio line, "WE DON'T CHASE THE HYPE". It is a real stance and most dessert bars do not have one.

sections.label: Front door
title: Three things people
meet first.
Three things
people meet
first.

pins.quote: WE SCOOP THE REAL GOOD STUFF
pins.what: The bio makes a promise the profile never proves.
pins.why: You won the Asian gelato championship, and nothing on the profile says so.
pins.how: Lead with the title and the craft behind it, not the outlet list.
pins.label: Your bio
pins.cost: New customers pick the viral brand because they never learn why yours is better.

pins.what: The highlights are mostly other brands' names.
pins.why: A row of collabs tells a young visitor Latteria borrows attention instead of owning it.
pins.how: Give highlights to your own story: the championship, the makers, the flavours.
pins.label: Your highlights
pins.cost: The generation you lost keeps meeting Latteria as a sidekick.

pins.area: Three grid posts in three unrelated typefaces and styles
pins.what: Each post wears a different typeface and mood.
pins.why: Your first customers are parents now, and the grid gives their children nothing to recognise.
pins.how: Pick one visual voice and hold it across every post and outlet.
pins.label: Your grid
pins.cost: Every new post starts from zero instead of adding to Latteria.

sections.intro: You asked for a look at Latteria, and you told me the brand no longer matches the gelato. I spent time on your Instagram. Three things stood out, and all three point the same way.

sections.body: It is 20 minutes with me. We go through this page together, on Latteria's own screens, and you leave knowing what to change first.
sections.note: A few short questions first, then you pick a time. You can also just reply to the email.

reference: Pierre Hermé, from pastry. It sells the maker's craft first, so every new trend looks like a copy next to it.
